teams.heading: Joji Nasova remains with Fijian Drua after Newcastle transfer collapses
teams.body: Fijian wing Joji Nasova will remain with the Fijian Drua after his planned transfer to Premiership side Newcastle Red Bulls was cancelled. The 25-year-old Olympic silver medallist, who has scored four tries in three appearances for Fiji, was released from his contract due to personal reasons. Newcastle general manager Neil McIlroy confirmed the club "fully understand and respect" Nasova's circumstances, prioritising the player's community ties.

lead.why: The collapse of Olympic silver medallist Joji Nasova's high-profile move to Premiership club Newcastle is a major talking point for Fiji fans.

teams.heading: Ellis Genge challenges England to 'cause some pain' in fiery pre-match footage
teams.body: Footage from the latest O2 Inside Line episode has captured vice-captain Ellis Genge delivering a fiery, expletive-laden address to the squad before the victory over Argentina. Genge urged teammates to 'cause some pain' and 'right the wrongs' of the campaign, citing the emotional spillover from England’s midweek football World Cup semi-final defeat to the Pumas. The speech preceded a fractious second half in which Steve Borthwick's side navigated four overlapping yellow cards to secure the win.

teams.heading: Matt Williams claims Ireland are well below the required elite standards
teams.body: Former head coach Matt Williams has criticised Ireland’s recent performances, describing the side as having been "publicly examined and exposed" during their Nations Championship campaign. Following the 40-21 defeat to New Zealand, Williams dismissed external excuses for the result, pointing to 18 turnovers and 35 missed tackles as evidence that defensive intensity was "well below elite standards." Andy Farrell has acknowledged the need to address these recurring errors, noting that his team must now reassess ahead of future fixtures.

teams.heading: High Court hears arguments to dismiss rugby brain injury legal claims
teams.body: The High Court has heard applications from rugby’s governing bodies to dismiss hundreds of brain injury claims currently brought against them. Legal representatives for the governing bodies argued that the cases should be thrown out, maintaining their position as the litigation continues to navigate the judicial process. This follows a period of upheaval for the claimants, who have recently sought new legal representation to advance their pursuit of compensation for long-term neurological conditions allegedly caused by their involvement in the sport.

lead.why: The ongoing High Court proceedings concerning brain injury litigation remain the most significant unresolved matter involving the sport's governing bodies.

While a signature win against the top-tier powers remains elusive, the squad’s consistency—including a narrow push against the Springboks—has earned them praise alongside the world champions, with Pierre Schoeman reinforcing the belief that the team has established itself as a genuine top-five international force.

teams.heading: Jac Morgan insists Wales are closing the gap to world's best
teams.body: Despite the chastening 43-0 defeat in Durban, flanker Jac Morgan maintains that Wales are making tangible progress under coach Steve Tandy. While the result in South Africa highlighted the current disparity in resources, Morgan pointed to recent performances against Scotland and Ireland in the Six Nations, along with the opening-round victory over Fiji, as evidence of development. The squad continues to prioritise integration and experience as they prepare for the November series and the following year's World Cup.

teams.heading: Tomas Albornoz faces misconduct charges following referee abuse after England defeat
teams.body: Fly-half Tomas Albornoz has been issued with misconduct charges by World Rugby following the aftermath of the 31-24 loss to England. Albornoz was seen remonstrating with official Angus Gardner after a late try for Bautista Delguy was disallowed. Nigel Owens has since criticised the conduct of both players and fans—who threw objects at the officiating team—calling the abuse "totally, totally unacceptable" and insisting that such behaviour must be dealt with strictly to maintain the standards of the game.

teams.heading: Les Kiss recalls Lukhan Salakaia-Loto for his first Wallabies squad
teams.body: New head coach Les Kiss has signalled a fresh start by recalling forward Lukhan Salakaia-Loto in his debut 34-man squad. Following a "robust conversation" among coaching staff, Kiss has opted for the powerhouse while stressing that no player is guaranteed a spot in the side. The group will prepare for the upcoming Japan series, with Kiss opting for "evolution not revolution" by retaining captain Harry Wilson. The squad includes Reds centre Isaac Henry as the sole uncapped player following Len Ikitau’s injury.

lead.why: The recall of Lukhan Salakaia-Loto highlights the start of the Les Kiss era and his new selection philosophy.

teams.heading: Les Kiss names Reds centre Isaac Henry in Wallabies squad update
teams.body: New Wallabies head coach Les Kiss has confirmed his 34-man squad for the upcoming two-Test series against Japan, headlined by the inclusion of uncapped Reds centre Isaac Henry. The selection follows confirmation that star centre Len Ikitau has been ruled out due to an ankle injury. Kiss noted that his coaching group prioritised form and cohesion for this series. “Selection is always a challenging process, but as coaches we’ve looked to bring together a group based on form,” said Kiss.

teams.heading: All Blacks legend Ma'a Nonu signs short-term deal with the Sharks
teams.body: The Durban club has confirmed that All Blacks legend Ma'a Nonu will continue his professional career in South Africa after signing a short-term deal. The 44-year-old double World Cup winner, who recently completed a successful spell at RC Toulon, will join the franchise to provide mentorship and leadership to their young centres. Nonu, who spent time back in New Zealand before making his decision, is expected to play a key role in developing talent like Jurenzo Julius.

teams.heading: Pieter-Steph du Toit defines Rassie Erasmus’ shift toward positional skill fusion
teams.body: South Africa’s recent performances have solidified a trend where jersey numbers are treated as administrative conveniences rather than rigid job specifications. Pieter-Steph du Toit epitomised this in July, seamlessly rotating through lock and back-row roles across three Tests without a dip in standards. Rassie Erasmus, alongside his peers in France and New Zealand, is prioritising a fusion of skill sets to match specific match requirements. This approach allowed the Springboks to maintain total dominance while rotating their personnel throughout the tournament.
